text:
maria zhang: FYI — CustX sent back their security questionnaire. Top asks: tenant KMS key rotation with proof-of-rotation, SIEM-friendly audit exports, and an incident response runbook for Private deployments. Can we put together talking points?

jamal singh: do they want key escrow or just a verification artifact?

maria zhang: they asked for both — they want to keep their own key material if possible, but also want a signed log that proves we served with rotated keys and which principal triggered the rotation.

alex harris: we can provide rotation attestations as an append-only signed manifest + hash chain. probably need to add a small RBAC tweak: a dedicated "kms-rotation" service account per-tenant so rotations are auditable.

natalie chen: agree. that avoids conflating operator creds with automation. @jamal can you check whether Dedicated/Private already issues per-tenant service accounts?

jamal singh: quick check — Dedicated yes, Private depends on customer infra (if they bring their own KMS we don't create service accounts in their KMS). For Private with Redwood-managed KMS we already create per-tenant service principals.

rohit patel: two practical gaps to call out to the customer: 1) log chain-of-custody for HSM-backed keys (we can export signed key-change events but HSM attestation requires customer to request an HSM audit report), 2) SIEM-friendly export — we can push to their S3/Syslog/Splunk via secure forwarder but retention/format needs config.

alex harris: sample audit export snippet to include in the response (format we propose):

```json
{
  "tenant_id": "custx-123",
  "event_type": "kms_key_rotation",
  "rotated_by": "service-account:kms-rotator:custx-123",
  "rotation_time": "2025-11-02T18:24:37Z",
  "rotation_manifest_sig": "sha256:abcdef...",
  "hsm_attestation": "optional, provided upon request"
}
```

natalie chen: good. also include the IR timeline we can commit to for Private deployments: acknowledge (15m), initial triage (1h), scope containment (4h), forensic artifact collection (24h). We should note that forensic collection for customer-managed on-prem KMS will require coordination and may add latency.

maria zhang: can we produce a short checklist for the questionnaire that they can slot into their compliance tracker?

jamal singh: yes — I'll draft a checklist. Items: confirm per-tenant service account, retention policy (default 90d logs), signed rotation manifests retained for 1 year, export destinations supported (S3/Splunk/Syslog), IR SLAs and contact sync, proof-of-rotation sample.

rohit patel: add a vuln-triage note: if rotation is triggered due to key compromise, we also rotate dependent model secrets and invalidate KV caches that reference the old keys. That should be in the runbook.

alex harris: posted a link to the runbook template in the draft answers — Deploy-bot can you attach the current IR runbook URL?

deploy-bot: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/ir-private-deployments|IR runbook (private)> :paperclip:

natalie chen: thanks — once Jamal posts the checklist and a short blurb about RBAC change, I'll assemble the questionnaire response and loop in Legal for the HSM attestation language.

maria zhang: perfect. jamal, can you drop the checklist + one example rotation manifest by EOD?

jamal singh: on it. also flagging potential work: if CustX wants automated SIEM push to their on-prem Splunk we may need a small connector (work request).

rohit patel: noted. I'll estimate connector effort after seeing their Splunk endpoint details.

alex harris: last note — include a brief sample of logs showing a rotation event context so their auditors see the chain:```
Nov 02 18:24:37 redwood-kms[rotator]: tenant=custx-123 event=kms_key_rotation new_key_id=key-09f3 rotated_by=service-account:kms-rotator:custx-123 manifest_sig=sha256:abcdef...
Nov 02 18:24:38 redwood-audit: tenant=custx-123 event=access_grant subject=sa:ingest:syslog request_id=zz-123
```

maria zhang: this is great, thanks team. I'll wait for Jamal's checklist and then we'll send the initial draft to CustX security. :thumbsup:
